claim: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are neuronal sodium-selective channels activated by reductions in extracellular pH.
source: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are neuronal sodium-selective channels activated by reductions in extracellular pH.
evidence: This is a well-established characterization of ASICs found in the abstract and introduction, representing established scientific knowledge about these channels.

claim: Structures of the three presumptive functional states (high-pH resting, low-pH desensitized, and toxin-stabilized open) have all been solved for chicken ASIC1.
source: Structures of the three presumptive functional states, high-pH resting, low-pH desensitized, and toxin-stabilized open, have all been solved for chicken ASIC1.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies in the manuscript (Baconguis et al., 2014; Baconguis and Gouaux, 2012; Gonzales et al., 2009; Jasti et al., 2007; Yoder et al., 2018).

claim: The isomerization or flipping of the β11–12 linker in the extracellular, ligand-binding domain is an integral component of the desensitization process.
source: These structures, along with prior functional data, suggest that the isomerization or flipping of the β11–12 linker in the extracellular, ligand-binding domain is an integral component of the desensitization process.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from structural data and prior functional studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: Both desensitization and recovery can be accelerated by orders of magnitude by mutating residues in the β11–12 linker or the surrounding region.
source: We find that both desensitization and recovery can be accelerated by orders of magnitude by mutating resides in this linker or the surrounding region.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, particularly the electrophysiology experiments on mutants.

claim: Desensitization can be suppressed by trapping the linker in the resting state.
source: Furthermore, desensitization can be suppressed by trapping the linker in the resting state, indicating that isomerization of the β11–12 linker is not merely a consequence of, but a necessity for the desensitization process in ASICs.
evidence: This claim is supported by the UV-trapping experiments with non-canonical amino acids presented in the manuscript.

claim: Isomerization of the β11–12 linker is a necessity for the desensitization process in ASICs.
source: Furthermore, desensitization can be suppressed by trapping the linker in the resting state, indicating that isomerization of the β11–12 linker is not merely a consequence of, but a necessity for the desensitization process in ASICs.
evidence: This claim is supported by inference from the UV-trapping experiments showing that preventing linker movement prevents desensitization.

claim: ASICs are a family of sodium-selective trimeric ion channels activated by extracellular acidification.
source: Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are a family of sodium-selective trimeric ion channels activated by extracellular acidification.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ASIC structure and function.

claim: The ASIC family is composed of four genes (five in humans) giving rise to six proton-sensitive isoforms.
source: This family is composed of four genes (five in humans) giving rise to six proton-sensitive isoforms which each have their own distinct expression profiles and biophysical properties (Gründer and Pusch, 2015; Kellenberger and Schild, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to review articles about ASIC family composition.

claim: Genetic studies have uncovered roles for ASICs in ischemic stroke, visceral pain sensation, epilepsy, substance abuse and fear conditioning.
source: Genetic studies have uncovered a variety of roles for ASICs such as in ischemic stroke, visceral pain sensation, epilepsy, substance abuse and fear conditioning (Kellenberger and Schild, 2015; Lin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on ASIC physiological roles.

claim: At physiological pH, ASICs are primarily found in a resting conformation.
source: At physiological pH, ASICs are primarily found in a resting conformation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ASIC behavior at physiological pH.

claim: A rapid drop in extracellular pH triggers ASIC activation and desensitization, occurring over several milliseconds and hundreds of milliseconds, respectively.
source: A rapid drop in extracellular pH triggers ASIC activation and desensitization, occurring over several milliseconds and hundreds of milliseconds, respectively (Du et al., 2014; Kreple et al., 2014; MacLean and Jayaraman, 2016; MacLean and Jayaraman, 2017; Wemmie et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies characterizing ASIC kinetics.

claim: Proposed structures for each of the resting, open and desensitized states have been solved by X-ray crystallography for the chicken ASIC1 isoform.
source: Proposed structures for each of the resting, open and desensitized states have been solved by X-ray crystallography for the chicken ASIC1 isoform (cASIC1) (Baconguis et al., 2014; Baconguis and Gouaux, 2012; Gonzales et al., 2009; Jasti et al., 2007; Yoder et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: ASICs are trimers with each subunit consisting of short intracellular N and C termini, two transmembrane helices and a large extracellular domain.
source: These structural studies reveal ASICs to be trimers with each subunit consisting of short intracellular N and C termini, two transmembrane helices and a large extracellular domain.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: The extracellular domain (ECD) has been likened to a hand, with finger, knuckle, thumb, palm and β-ball domains.
source: The extracellular domain (ECD) has been likened to a hand, with finger, knuckle, thumb, palm and β-ball domains (Figure 1A; Jasti et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and reference to Figure 1A showing the structure.

claim: In the open and desensitized structures, the upper half of the ECD is nearly identical while the lower half and the transmembrane domains show substantial differences.
source: Interestingly, in the open and desensitized structures, the upper half of the ECD is nearly identical while the lower half and the transmembrane domains show substantial differences (Baconguis and Gouaux, 2012; Yoder et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies comparing open and desensitized states.

claim: In the resting and desensitized structures, the lower ECD and transmembrane domain conformations are similar while the upper ECD is distinct.
source: However, in the resting and desensitized structures, the lower ECD and transmembrane domain conformations are similar while the upper ECD is distinct.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of structural data from cited studies.

claim: The transition zone between the upper ECD and the lower ECD is marked by the linker between β-strands 11 and 12.
source: The transition zone between the upper ECD, similar in open and desensitized states, and the lower ECD, similar in resting and desensitized states, is marked by the linker between β-strands 11 and 12.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from structural comparisons.

claim: Leu414 and Asn415 are particularly important as mutations to these highly conserved residues have been reported to alter desensitization kinetics and activation curves.
source: Within this linker, Leu414 and Asn415 (chicken numbering) are known to be particularly important as mutations to these highly conserved residues have been reported to alter desensitization kinetics and activation curves (Li et al., 2010a; Roy et al., 2013; Springauf et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to functional studies of these mutations.

claim: In open (and resting) structures, the side chain of Leu414 is oriented outwards, away from the central axis of the channel, and forms a hydrophobic contact with Leu86.
source: In open (and resting) structures, the side chain of Leu414 is oriented outwards, away from the central axis of the channel, and forms a hydrophobic contact with Leu86 (Baconguis et al., 2014; Baconguis and Gouaux, 2012; Yoder et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: In the desensitized state, Leu414 and Asn415 swap orientations, with Leu414 pointing downwards and Asn415 swinging up.
source: However, in the desensitized state the residues swap orientations, with Leu414 pointing downwards and Asn415 swinging up (Figure 1B; Gonzales et al., 2009; Jasti et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to structural studies and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The β11–12 linker acts as a 'molecular clutch', coupling the conformational changes in the acidic pocket to the TMD, driving activation and subsequently disengaging during desensitization.
source: This substantial motion, as well as past functional data, has prompted the suggestion that this linker acts as a 'molecular clutch', coupling the conformational changes in the acidic pocket to the TMD, driving activation and subsequently disengaging during desensitization, enabling the upper ECD to maintain a protonated conformation yet simultaneously allowing the lower ECD and TMDs to collapse and adopt a resting-like conformation (Baconguis and Gouaux, 2012; Yoder et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is a hypothesis supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: cASIC1 essentially completely desensitized with a time constant of 181 ± 6 ms.
source: We initially examined the recovery time course of cASIC1 wild type and found that cASIC1 essentially completely desensitized with a time constant of 181 ± 6 ms (Figure 1C,E–F)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The L414A mutation underwent faster desensitization (41 ± 1 ms, n = 5, p<1e−5 vs wild type).
source: Consistent with our hypothesis that a smaller residue in the Leu414 position would be more nimble and subject to less steric hindrance, the L414A mutation underwent faster desensitization (41 ± 1 ms, n = 5, p<1e−5 vs wild type)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing L414A to wild type.

claim: L414A in human ASIC1a slows or attenuates desensitization and right shifts proton activation curves.
source: Recently, Wu et al. (2019) reported that L414A in human ASIC1a slows or attenuates desensitization, as well as right shifts proton activation curves.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wu et al. 2019.

claim: L414A in cASIC1 produced only a small shift in the pH50 of activation compared to wild type (wild type: pH50act = 6.57 ± 0.03, n = 5; L414A: pH50act = 6.43 ± 0.03, n = 6, p=0.027).
source: Consistent with the lack of motion of Leu414 between resting and open states, but in contrast to previous reports, we observed only a small shift in the pH50 of activation for L414A compared to wild type (wild type: pH50act = 6.57 ± 0.03, n = 5; L414A: pH50act = 6.43 ± 0.03, n = 6, p=0.027).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from pH dose-response experiments.

claim: The desensitization of L414A is incomplete and a sustained current develops with pH values less than 5.
source: However, we did observe that the desensitization of Leu414A is incomplete and a sustained current develops with pH values less than 5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Non-stationary fluctuation analysis indicated a peak Popen of 0.86 ± 0.02 (n = 5) for cASIC1 wild type.
source: The NSFA indicated a peak Popen of 0.86 ± 0.02 (n = 5, Figure 2C) with an estimated single channel conductance of 10 ± 1 pS, consistent with previously published conductance data (Lynagh et al., 2017; Zhang and Canessa, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from NSFA shown in Figure 2.

claim: This represents the first estimate of the open probability of recombinant ASICs.
source: Importantly, to our knowledge, this represents the first estimate of the open probability of recombinant ASICs.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the measurement, based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: NSFA of L414A containing patches yielded a significantly reduced peak Popen of 0.71 ± 0.02 (n = 5, p<1e−5 versus wild type).
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, NSFA of L414A containing patches yielded a significantly reduced peak Popen of 0.71 ± 0.02 (n = 5, p<1e−5 versus wild type, Figure 2) with minimal change in single channel conductance (16 ± 2 pS, p=0.03 versus wild type).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from NSFA shown in Figure 2.

claim: The reduced peak open probability in L414A is consistent with ASICs desensitizing primarily from closed states.
source: This result is consistent with ASICs desensitizing primarily from closed states.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation of reduced peak open probability.

claim: The chosen protonation scheme stabilizes the desensitized state better than the deprotonated state.
source: From Figure 3—figure supplement 1, it is clear that the chosen protonation scheme (orange) stabilizes the structure better than the deprotonated state (blue), both when looking at the full protein structure and in particular when only including the extracellular domain.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: L414A mutation produces a slight increase in the RMSD of the β11–12 linker region in protonated simulations.
source: This analysis found a slight increase in the RMSD of the surrounding area induced by the L414A (Figure 3A, middle).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Upon deprotonation, increased RMSD of the linker region was observed for one chain in wild-type simulations and three chains in L414A simulations.
source: Upon deprotonation, we observed increased RMSD of the linker region for the wild type in three of the chains, while for the L414A mutant, six chains displayed increased RMSD values for the linker region relative to the protonated case.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: The L414A mutation increased the flexibility of the middle part of the β11–12 linker in deprotonated simulations.
source: From RMSF calculations, it was also evident that the L414A mutation increased the flexibility of the middle part of the linker (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: ASIC recovery from desensitization depends on the pH separating the paired pulses.
source: However, ASIC recovery from desensitization has been reported to depend on the pH separating the paired pulses (Immke and McCleskey, 2003; MacLean and Jayaraman, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Recovery from desensitization was slower when using pH 7.8 and 7.6 as the inter pulse pH compared to pH 8.
source: We observed a similar effect where the recovery from desensitization was slower when using pH 7.8 and 7.6 as the inter pulse pH (τrecovery pH 7.8: 1600 ± 90 ms, m = 0.83 ± 0.01, n = 5, p=0.005 versus pH 8; pH 7.6: 11400 ± 600 ms, m = 0.73 ± 0.03, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus pH 8, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Alkalinizing the interpulse pH to pH 9 dramatically accelerated recovery in wild type channels (τ = 30 ± 2 ms, m = 3.0 ± 0.1, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus pH 8).
source: Interestingly, alkalinizing the interpulse pH was able to dramatically accelerate recovery in wild type channels. Specifically, when using pH 9, channels recovered with a time constant of 30 ± 2 ms (m = 3.0 ± 0.1, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus pH 8)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Recovery accelerated to 7.5 ± 0.4 ms (m = 5.3 ± 0.3, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus pH 8) with pH 10 interpulse.
source: and this accelerated to 7.5 ± 0.4 ms (m = 5.3 ± 0.3, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus pH 8) with pH 10 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: L414A retained very fast recovery at pH 8, 7.8 and 7.6 with a slight but significant slowing at pH 7.6.
source: We found that L414A retained very fast recovery at all pH's tested with a slight but significant slowing when using an inter-pulse pH of pH 7.6 (τrecovery pH 7.8: 3.4 ± 0.4 ms, m = 10 ± 2, n = 6; pH 7.6: 8.4 ± 0.6 ms, m = 3.7 ± 0.2, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus pH 8, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The side chain of L414 interacted with E80, A82, Q277, L281, Y283, I306, M364, V368 and R370 in simulations of the protonated desensitized state.
source: In our simulations of the protonated desensitized state, we noted that the side chain of L414 interacted with the side chains of E80, A82, Q277, L281, Y283, I306, M364, V368 and R370 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: All Ala mutations to hydrophobic residues L281, I306, M364 and V368 significantly accelerated recovery from desensitization.
source: We found that all Ala mutations significantly accelerated recovery from desensitization, and most cases the effect was substantial.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on the hydrophobic patch mutations.

claim: L281A recovery time constant was 25 ± 1.1 ms (m = 3.9 ± 0.2, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus wild type).
source: Specifically, the time constants (and slopes) for recovery from desensitization for L281A, I306A, M364A and V368A were 25 ± 1.1 (m = 3.9 ± 0.2, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus wild type)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: I306A recovery time constant was 135 ± 7 ms (m = 1.31 ± 0.04, n = 5, p<1e−5 versus wild type).
source: 135 ± 7 (m = 1.31 ± 0.04,n = 5, p<1e−5 versus wild type)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: M364A recovery time constant was 140 ± 3 ms (m = 1.44 ± 0.02, n = 4, p<1e−5 versus wild type).
source: 140 ± 3 (m = 1.44 ± 0.02,n = 4, p<1e−5 versus wild type)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: V368A recovery time constant was 520 ± 50 ms (m = 0.99 ± 0.06, n = 5, p=0.01 versus wild type).
source: and 520 ± 50 ms (m = 0.99 ± 0.06, n = 5, p=0.01 versus wild type), respectively (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: L281A markedly increased the rate of channel desensitization (τdes = 47 ± 3 ms, p<1e−5 versus wild type).
source: Interestingly, L281A showed the largest acceleration of recovery but also markedly increased the rate of channel desensitization (τdes =  47 ± 3 ms, p<1e−5 versus wild type).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: I306A and M364A did not substantially alter desensitization (τdes = 240 ± 11; 108 ± 3 ms, respectively).
source: However, I306A and M364A did not substantially alter desensitization (τdes =  240 ± 11; 108 ± 3 ms, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The double I306A/M364A mutation did not exhibit an increased effect on recovery compared to the single mutations (τrecovery 110 ± 9 ms, m = 1.37 ± 0.03, n = 5).
source: However, this double mutation did not exhibit an increased effect on recovery as compared to the single mutations (τrecovery 110 ± 9 ms, m = 1.37 ± 0.03, n = 5, Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: No simple rule of size or polarity is sufficient to explain or predict the effects of mutations at position 414.
source: Based on this surprising set of results, particularly the dramatic acceleration by the bulky Tyr residue and the notable effect of the conservative Ile substitution, we conclude that no simple rule of size or polarity is sufficient to explain or predict the effects of this position as yet.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on various mutations at position 414.

claim: In the simulations of the wild type deprotonated protein, L414 and N415 seemed to come close to flipping in one chain, following the outwards path, but the conformation reverted back before completing the flip.
source: Two of these showed no signs of flips, while for the third chain, L414 and N415 seemed to come close to flipping, following the outwards path as originally suggested by Yoder et al. (2018); however, the conformation reverted back to the desensitized conformation before completing the flip.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: In the deprotonated L414A mutant, five of nine chains underwent at least a 'partial flip'.
source: Finally, in agreement with L414A increasing flexibility of the β11–12 linker, elevated RMSD values for the linker region are observed for six of the nine chains for the deprotonated L414A mutant. One of these chains showed no signs of flipping, while the other five chains underwent at least a 'partial flip' (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: A full flip was observed for one chain in the deprotonated L414A simulations, in which the outwards path was followed for both residues.
source: Finally, the full flip was observed for one chain in which a very good overlay with the resting conformation of the linker was obtained (Video 1). In this trajectory, the outwards path was followed for both residues.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Video 1.

claim: The molecular dynamics simulations support the original suggestion of an outwards path for both L414 and N415.
source: Hence, while we would need more repeats and more full flips to get conclusive data, our work supports the original suggestion of an outwards path for both L414 and N415.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: UV application to L414Bpa during the resting state produced a strong and immediate slowing of desensitization and robustly reduced the extent of desensitization (Iss/Ipeak, n = 7, p<1e−5 between pre and post-UV).
source: As seen in Figure 7, such UV application produced a strong and immediate slowing of desensitization and robustly reduced the extent of desensitization (Iss/Ipeak, n = 7, p<1e−5 between pre and post-UV)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Cells transfected with cASIC1_GFP L414TAG plus R3 but without MeO-Bpa did not exhibit UV modulation (n = 4, p=0.7 between pre and post UV).
source: Crucially, these cells did not exhibit UV modulation (n = 4, p=0.7 between pre and post UV) nor did responses from cells expressing wild-type cASIC_GFP (n = 3, p=0.6 between pre and post UV), indicating the UV effect was specific to the incorporated Bpa (Figure 7B and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Cells expressing wild-type cASIC_GFP did not exhibit UV modulation (n = 3, p=0.6 between pre and post UV).
source: nor did responses from cells expressing wild-type cASIC_GFP (n = 3, p=0.6 between pre and post UV), indicating the UV effect was specific to the incorporated Bpa (Figure 7B and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Trapping the conformation of the 414 position in the resting state substantially reduces the capacity of the channel to undergo desensitization but does not preclude activation.
source: These data indicate that trapping the conformation of the 414 position in the resting state substantially reduces the capacity of the channel to undergo desensitization but does not preclude activation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the UV-trapping experiments.

claim: The current rise times following UV application changed (10–90% rise time: before UV, 12 ± 1 ms; post UV, 830 ± 400 ms, n = 7, p<1e−5 between pre- and post-UV).
source: Interestingly, the current rise times following UV application did change (10–90% rise time: before UV, 12 ± 1 ms; post UV, 830 ± 400 ms, n = 7, p<1e−5 between pre- and post-UV, Figure 7C), indicating some rearrangements near the β11–12 linker accompany channel activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: UV application to desensitized L414Bpa channels inhibited peak responses by approximately 50% (47 ± 4% peak response, n = 6).
source: As seen in Figure 8, UV application to desensitized channels inhibited peak responses by approximately 50% (47 ± 4% peak response, n = 6, Figure 8)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: UV application to desensitized wild-type cASIC1_GFP transfected cells did not inhibit peak responses (96 ± 3% peak response, n = 3).
source: which was not observed in recordings from either wild-type cASIC1_GFP transfected cells (96 ± 3% peak response, n = 3)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: UV application to desensitized cASIC1_GFP L414TAG transfected cells without MeO-Bpa did not inhibit peak responses (91 ± 8% peak response, n = 3).
source: or in cASIC1_GFP L414TAG transfected cells when MeO-Bpa was omitted (91 ± 8% peak response, n = 3, Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The Leu414 position undergoes a sizeable motion between resting/open and desensitized states.
source: Combined with the results of the resting state trapping experiments (Figure 7), these data are clear evidence that the Leu414 position undergoes a sizeable motion between resting/open and desensitized states.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the UV-trapping experiments in both resting and desensitized states.

claim: The β11–12 linker is the sole mechanism for channel desensitization.
source: Furthermore, the sizeable attenuation of macroscopic desensitization by resting state trapping experiments (Figure 7) argues that this β11–12 linker is the sole mechanism for channel desensitization.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the resting state UV-trapping experiments.

claim: The β11–12 linker and surrounding areas act as a switch or clutch to control the desensitization process of ASICs.
source: Based on our and previous work, it is clear that the β11–12 linker and surrounding areas act as a switch or clutch (Yoder et al., 2018) to control the desensitization process of ASICs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and previous work.

claim: The data provides support for an outwards transit path for L414 and N415 when undergoing the conformational 'flip'.
source: While our data provides support for an outwards transit path for L414 and N415 when undergoing the suggested conformational 'flip', many of the precise molecular details remain unclear.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: cASIC1 does not undergo the strong tachyphylaxis mammalian ASIC1a does in outside out patches.
source: Second, in our hands, cASIC1 does not undergo the strong tachyphylaxis mammalian ASIC1a does in outside out patches (Chen and Gründer, 2007).
evidence: This is an observation from the authors' experiments, supported by citation to a study on ASIC1a tachyphylaxis.

claim: The pH-dependence of the sustained current in L414A is comparable to that reported for L414A activation in oocytes.
source: Interestingly, the pH-dependence of this sustained current is comparable to that reported for L414A activation in oocytes (Roy et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the authors' data to previous reports.

claim: Past experiments with L414A and similar mutations have probably reported the pH sensitivity of the emerging sustained current while the peak current would have desensitized too quickly to adequately resolve.
source: Therefore, past experiments with this, and likely other mutations with similar phenotypes, have probably reported the pH sensitivity of the emerging sustained current while the peak current would have desensitized too quickly to adequately resolve.
evidence: This is speculation based on the authors' observations and comparison to previous reports.

claim: The activation times of 'fast' mutants were generally faster than wild type (10–90% rise time: wt, 7 ± 3 ms, n = 15; L414A, 4 ± 1 ms, n = 11; L414Y 1.0 ± 0.3, n = 4).
source: However, we did observe that the activation times of these 'fast' mutants were generally faster than wild type (10–90% rise time: wt, 7 ± 3 ms, n = 15; L414A, 4 ± 1 ms, n = 11; L414Y 1.0 ± 0.3, n = 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The slope of the L414A pH activation curve is shallower than that of wild-type cASIC1.
source: Finally, the slope of the L414A pH activation curve is shallower than that of wild-type cASIC1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: There are likely some local re-arrangements of the β11–12 loop during the resting to open transition which Leu414 can regulate.
source: Thus, there are likely some local re-arrangements of the β11–12 loop during the resting to open transition which Leu414 can regulate; however, these re-arrangements comprise a smaller portion of the energy barrier than was previously proposed.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on activation kinetics and UV-trapping.

claim: If the prime determinant of desensitization is the size of the 277 side chain, then one would expect Gln277 to behave identically to Glu277, and Asn277 to be identical to Asp277.
source: First, if the prime determinant of desensitization is the size of the 277 side chain, then one would expect Gln277 to behave identically to Glu277, and Asn277 to be identical to Asp277.
evidence: This is a logical inference used to critique the 'valve' model.

claim: Mutations bearing acidic side chains at position 277 show slower/reduced extent of desensitization than their amide counterparts.
source: However, mutations bearing the acidic side chains show slower/reduced extent of desensitization than their amide counter parts, hinting at a role for electrostatic interactions (Wu et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wu et al. 2019.

claim: A clear transit path is observed along the outward trajectory proposed by Yoder et al. but not the inward route posited by Wu et al. when examining calculated surfaces of the open and desensitized states.
source: However, examining the calculated surfaces of the open (or resting) and desensitized states, a clear transit path is observed along the outward trajectory proposed by Yoder et al. but not the inward route posited by Wu et al.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from structural analysis.

claim: In molecular dynamic simulations repeats where β11–12 flipping is observed, a clear outward transit for the 414 and 415 side chains is generally seen.
source: Third, in our molecular dynamic simulations repeats where β11–12 flipping is observed, we generally see a clear outward transit for the 414 and 415 side chains (Video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Video 1.

claim: The side chain conformation of Gln277 is relatively stable in the simulations with protonated states.
source: While the side chain conformation of Gln277 is relatively stable in the simulations with protonated states, as judged from the χ1- χ3 side chain dihedral angles (Figure 9), a number of changes in the side chain conformations are observed.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 9.

claim: Conformational flexibility of Gln277 occasionally causes its side chain to move outside of hydrogen bond distance between Gln277Nε and Leu414O.
source: Such conformational flexibility of Gln277 occasionally causes its side chain to move outside of hydrogen bond distance between Gln277Nε and Leu414O (Figure 9).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 9.

claim: L414A does not show a dramatic slowing of deactivation or a resurgent current following agonist removal.
source: We observed neither of these phenomena in L414A (Figure 1C,D) or any other fast recovering mutant in our study, suggesting that ASICs more likely recover from low pH desensitization by passing through closed states and not open states.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data used to infer the recovery pathway.

claim: ASICs more likely recover from low pH desensitization by passing through closed states and not open states.
